lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Not yet. A hunter does not walk into the lodge with empty hands.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Your spear is at Oren's forge, your herbs are at Mira's hut. Then come back.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Grik. You came.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Every hunter of Sundrop has stood where you stand. Today you face the Three Trials of the Hunter.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The first: read the land. A thornback boar has been tearing up the Wildwood. Find its trail and bring it down.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The second: feed the village. A hunter fills the stores, not just his own belly.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The third: face the king of beasts. When you reach it, you will know.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Don't worry, Father. If he comes back with a rabbit, we'll call it a very small boar.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Drogg.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Quiet. Yes.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The Wildwood is east, past the river. Go, and come back a hunter.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The thornback beds down in the Wildwood. Read its trail before you chase it.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: A hunter who runs in blind comes home carried.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: You found it. Tracked it. Brought it down.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Lirra helped me read the signs.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Then you also learned to listen. Good.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The first trial. Passed.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The second trial is not a fight. A hunter feeds the village, and Mira's winter stores are short. Go and ask her what she needs.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: A hunter feeds the village, not his pride. Bring Mira what she needs.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The Boar King of Silverpine. My father faced it, and I faced it. Now it is your turn.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Drogg is waiting at the crossroads. Go.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Drogg came through the gate singing. The whole village heard him. Half of them followed him here.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The Boar King of Silverpine. You read the land, you fed the village, and you faced the king of beasts.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Kneel, Grik.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: By the Three Trials, you are a hunter of Sundrop. Your name goes on the lodge wall, beside mine and my father's.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: This knife was the first I ever carried. It is yours now. Keep it sharp, and never draw it for pride.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Father, I...

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Go home. Tikka has been cooking since noon, and if we are late, she will make us regret it.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Take a few coins too. Oren will want to see what a real hunter buys.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: The lodge stands because its hunters come home. Mind that you do.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Grik! Get back! They are in the lanes, behind you. Drive them away from the houses!

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Don't come to me until the lanes are clear. Go!

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Grik...

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: No. Don't look at it. Look at me.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: They came over the bridge in the dark. So many. Their armour turns a spear like it is nothing.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: I held the gate as long as I could. It was not long enough.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Your brother went after Tikka. Toward the well. Find them, Grik.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: You are a hunter of Sundrop. Your name is on the wall. Beside mine.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: I was so proud... today...

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Father.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: ...I'll find them. I promise.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: When your mother was alive, she used to say you would be the best of us. I told her you were too stubborn.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: She was right. I was also right.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Eat, Grik. Then listen to your grandfather. He has been waiting all day to tell you something.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Eat. You earned it.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: There he is. Father sent me to help carry the meat home. That's all. Not because he's worried.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: He's worried.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: He's terrified. Don't tell him I said that either.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: The Boar King roams Silverpine, north across the river. Old, huge, and meaner than Oren before breakfast.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Its trail starts past the bridge. Go and find it. I'll be right behind you.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: North, across the bridge into Silverpine. Look for the trail. You can't miss it. Trees don't usually lie down on their own.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Silverpine is that way. The scary way.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Hear that? It's up on the terrace. It knows we're here.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Listen, little brother. No jokes for once.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: When a beast that big comes at you, every part of you will want to back away. Don't. You can't outrun it backwards.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Step to the side. Let it pass. Strike while it turns. That's all hunting is, really. Knowing where not to stand.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Drogg. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Don't make it strange. Go on. I'll be right here if it goes badly. Which it won't.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Up on the terrace. Sidestep, then strike. When it gets angry, and it will, keep your head.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Falls are loud. Good. Hides how hard my heart is beating.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Have I told you about the moment the Boar King charged? Grik didn't even flinch. Stepped aside like a dancer.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: You told everyone. Three times.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Then I'll tell them a fourth. It was the best thing I've ever seen, little brother. Honestly.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: If Tikka asks, I didn't take a second bowl.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Little brother! We were starting to think you'd run off to live with the rabbits.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Hurry up and get your gear. Father has been staring at the door like it owes him money.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Still here? The boar won't come to you, little brother. Though if it does, scream. I'd like to see that.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Picking moss! The fearsome hunter! I'll warn the village to lock up its mushrooms.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Fine, fine. Winter is long and fevers are worse. It matters. Don't tell Father I said that.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Father is talking about the old days again. Save me.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Little brother. You found me. Good, I was getting bored.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Don't look at that. It's nothing. It's... it's bad, Grik.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: They took Tikka. Lirra tried to pull her free, and they took her too. Dragged them both to the green, by the old signboard.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: There's a captain there. Sun on his chest. Big. Bigger than the Boar King.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: I'm not leaving you here.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: You are. Go. Sidestep, then strike. Remember?

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Go.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Go... Grik...

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Drogg. Hold on.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Grik, there are too many of them! Don't, please. Go!

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Oh! Grik. What a surprise. I was just picking herbs. Here. At the edge of the Wildwood. On your proving day.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Mira said you'd be here.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Mira says too much.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Well, since I'm here anyway. You're looking for a thornback, aren't you? I saw it cross the mouth of the forest at dawn.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Look for three signs: hoofprints in the mud, a sapling it smashed, and tusk scrapes on the bark. Read all three and you'll know where it sleeps.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: I'll keep up. Try not to step on anything that bites.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Hoofprints in the mud, a broken sapling, and tusk scrapes on the bark. Find all three.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: The wolves are restless this morning. If they come at you, don't run. They love it when you run.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: The trail goes north, up past the old cave. It will be bedded down in the high pocket.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Thornbacks charge when they're cornered. Keep a potion close.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: The Wildwood always looks friendlier from the village.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Here we are. Thank you for walking me home, hunter.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: You can just call me Grik.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Not tonight. Tonight you're a hunter.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Here. The arrow from the thornback. I've been carrying it all day. You should keep it. It belongs to the hunter who found it.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: It's just an orc arrow.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Then it's a lucky orc arrow. Keep it anyway.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Tomorrow. The river. Don't oversleep this time.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Goodnight, Grik. Tomorrow, remember.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Second trial already? You're getting faster.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Moonmoss glows faintly in the fog. Look for pale green light near the water. There are clumps scattered all through the basin.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: The marsh flowers are pretty. Don't smell them. I'm serious.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Four clumps. Follow the glow and stay on the firm ground.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: If the toads swell up, that's your cue to hit them first.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: That's all four? Then come and sit by the pond with me before we go back. Just for a moment. I'll meet you there.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: The fog hides everything out here. I like that, sometimes.

lines.speaker: Lodge Keeper
lines.text: Lodge stores. Rope, rations, and a few things the hunters left behind. Take what you need, pay what you owe.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Your herb pouch, hunter-to-be. Three field potions, mixed this morning.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Drink one when a wound will not close on its own. Do not wait until you are seeing two of everything.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Lirra was up before dawn too. She said she needed herbs from the Wildwood edge. Today. Of all days.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: I'm sure it's a coincidence.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Borak sent you? Good. A hunter who asks the herb-wife what the village needs. Your father taught him well, and he is teaching you.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The winter stores are short on moonmoss. It keeps fever away when the snow comes, and it grows only in the deep Mistfen.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Four clumps will see us through. Lirra knows the marsh better than anyone. She'll meet you at the Mistfen bridge, west of the village.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Mind the toads. They puff up when they're angry, and they are always angry.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Four clumps of moonmoss, from the deep Mistfen. Do you need anything for the road?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Four clumps, and not a leaf bruised. The village will sleep easier this winter.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: And Lirra came back smiling, which she does not do for moss.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Borak stopped by while you were out. The third trial is the Boar King of Silverpine. Drogg is waiting for you at the crossroads signpost.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: He told me to say it plainly, so I will: be careful, Grik.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Herbs, salves, and potions, all fresh. What will it be?

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: There he is. The last goblin in Sundrop to wake, on the one morning it matters.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Come here, boy. Bend down. My knees will not reach your neck.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: This amulet was my father's, and his mother's before him. It has hung on every hunter in our family since the old days.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: It will not stop a tusk. But it will remind you whose blood you carry. Wear it, and bring it home.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: I will, Grandfather.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Good. Oren has the spear your father ordered, and Mira has your herb pouch. Fetch them both before you go to Borak.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Sit by the fire, boy. A hunter should know where he comes from.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Long ago, the world was at peace. Goblins, orcs, elves, even the demons of the north. We traded, we feasted, we married into each other's clans. A long peace, longer than anyone could count.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Then a hero came across the sea. A human, with a sword that burned like the sun.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: He said the demons were a darkness on the world. And the humans who followed him believed him.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: The demons fell. All of them. And when there were no demons left, the humans looked at the rest of us, and they saw beasts.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: They called it the Great Hunt. Village after village burned. The ones who lived ran into the mountains and the deep woods.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: Father. Not tonight.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: He is a hunter now, Borak. He should know what hunts us.

lines.speaker: Borak
lines.text: He will. Not tonight.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: ...As you say.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: One more thing, boy. Under the shrine there is an old tunnel, sealed since before your father was born. No one goes in. No one. Do you understand?

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Yes, Grandfather.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Good. Now, your sister says Lirra is about to leave, and someone should walk her home.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Humans. Humans, in the village. I thought I would never see it again.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Your father and Drogg ran for the gate. Tikka went to the well for water before dawn. She has not come back.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Take your spear and your knife. Find them. Go!

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Grandfather, come with me...

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: My legs are too old to run, and too stubborn to hide. I will be at the shrine. Go!

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Back so soon? The Wildwood is east, past the river. The boar will not wait for you to finish napping.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Hm? Oh, don't mind me. I'm only resting my eyes. They've seen a great deal.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Easy. Easy, boy. You are in the shrine. I carried you here myself, so don't tell me I'm too old.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Father. Drogg. They...

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Tikka and Lirra. They took them. I have to...

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: You have to live. That is all you have to do tonight.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: The humans are searching every house. They will reach the shrine before the fire burns out.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Do you remember what I told you last night? The tunnel under the shrine. I told you no one goes in. Tonight, you do.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: It runs under the mountain and comes out in the Wildwood, past the old cave. Our ancestors dug it, when the Great Hunt came the first time.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: The tunnel is waiting, boy. Go.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Borak's boy! Your father paid for this a week ago and made me swear not to tell you.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: A practice spear. Ash shaft, iron head, balanced for a short arm. No offence.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Some offence.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Ha! Grow into it. Open your pack and equip it before you leave. A spear in a bag has never killed anything.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: If you come home with coin, come back. I keep better steel for real hunters.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Steel for those who can pay, advice for those who can't. Today, the advice is free.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Grik! No, don't! Run! Please, just run!

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Why are you still here? Spear from Oren, herbs from Mira, then the lodge. Even I know that, and I'm not the one being proved.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Sit! No, not there, that's Grandfather's spot. There. Good.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Drogg, plates. Father, stop sharpening that and pass the bread. Grik, you're a hunter now, so you can carry the stew pot.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: It's the boar, obviously. I've been stewing it all afternoon. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: I'm proud of you, by the way. Don't let it go to your head. You'll still do the dishes.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Lirra's leaving! Walk her back to the herb hut. Go on, hunter. Go!

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: You're home. Good. Bed, hunter. Big day tomorrow, Lirra says. She wouldn't tell me why.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: I'm making something good for tonight. No, you can't know what. Go and do your trials.

lines.speaker: Io
lines.text: When you're a real hunter, will you bring me a wolf tooth? A big one. Please?

lines.speaker: Io
lines.text: I'm going to be a hunter too, one day. Just like you.

lines.speaker: Lynn
lines.text: The proving hunt is today, isn't it? Good luck, Grik. Bring back something with more meat than bone.

lines.speaker: Lynn
lines.text: Sundrop is quiet today. I like quiet.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: My first proving, I tripped over my own spear in front of the whole lodge. Borak still tells that story.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: You'll do better. You can hardly do worse.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: My roof leaks, my goat bites, and my wife says I snore. Still, it's a good life.
Morning light slants through the gaps in the thatch. Somewhere outside, a rooster is losing an argument with a goat.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Grik. Grik! Get up!

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Mm. Five more breaths.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: Today is your proving hunt, you lump! Father and Drogg left for the lodge before the sun was up.

lines.speaker: Tikka
lines.text: If you make Father wait, he'll pretend he isn't angry. That's worse. Grandfather wants you by the hearth first. Go!
Deep, split hoofprints sink into the soft mud beside the trail.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Big. Heavy on the front feet.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: And fresh. See how the water hasn't filled them yet? It passed here this morning. Heading north.
A young birch lies snapped at knee height, its bark peeled back in long strips.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: It didn't go around. It went through.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: So it's angry.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Or it's something that has never needed to go around anything.
Pale gouges score an old oak, higher than Grik's head. Sap still weeps from them.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: It marks its ground up here. The bed is close.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Look at you, reading the land. Borak would almost smile.
The thornback lies still. Grik's hands are shaking, and he lets them.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Grik. Look at its flank.
A broken arrow is buried in the boar's hide, half grown over. The head is iron, the shaft is straight and planed, and the fletching is stamped with a small golden sun.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: That isn't ours. No goblin fletches like that.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Then who?

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: An orc caravan, probably. They come through the passes sometimes. It's nothing.
Lirra works the arrow free and tucks it into her satchel without a word.
The fog lies thick over the still water. For a while neither of them says anything.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Do you ever think about later? After you're a hunter, I mean.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: I'll hunt. I'll fill the stores. I'll get old and tell bad stories like Grandfather.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: That's not later. That's just more of today.

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: Tomorrow, after all this, come to the river with me. There's a place I want to show you. Just you.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: What kind of place?

lines.speaker: Lirra
lines.text: The kind you have to see. Now come on. Mira will think the toads ate us.
The trail is not a trail so much as a road. Saplings are flattened, stones are overturned, and the earth is churned into ridges.
Each hoofprint is wider than Grik's two hands spread together.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: It went up toward the falls.
From somewhere ahead, over the noise of the water, comes a low, grinding snort.
The Boar King sways, groans, and crashes into the moss. The ground shakes once, and then the forest is quiet.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: You did it. Grik, you actually did it!

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Wait until Father sees this. Wait until the whole village sees this!
Drogg heaves the great boar across his shoulders, staggers, laughs, and sets off down the mountain.

lines.speaker: Drogg
lines.text: Told you I came to carry the meat.
Grik lies awake for a long time, turning the sun-stamped arrow over in his fingers.
Through the wall he can hear Drogg snoring and Tikka telling him to stop. Old Mott hums an old song by the fire.
Tomorrow, the river.
He sleeps.
A horn. Then another, long and low, nothing like the hunting horns of Sundrop.
Smoke is coming in under the door. Outside, someone is screaming.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Grik! Up! Up, boy!
The world goes dark and quiet. Somewhere far away, a deep voice laughs.

lines.speaker: Captain
lines.text: Leave that one.

lines.speaker: Captain
lines.text: Don't waste a rope on him. The little one won't last long out here anyway.

lines.speaker: Captain
lines.text: Load the rest. We march south at first light.
Old Mott pulls a carved stone from the shrine floor. Cold air breathes up out of the dark.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Come with me.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Someone has to close the door behind you. I am the only one left who knows how.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Live, Grik. Remember us.

lines.speaker: Old Mott
lines.text: Now, this is your hunt.
Grik steps down into the dark. Behind him, stone grinds on stone. Then the ceiling roars, and the tunnel falls in.
The cave opens onto a high ridge above the Wildwood. Far below, beyond the river, Sundrop is a smudge of black smoke against the dawn.
On the southern road, a long line of soldiers marches away from the village. Between them, roped together, walk the goblins of Sundrop.
He can't see Tikka or Lirra. He looks until his eyes hurt.
Grik's hand finds something in his pack. Straight shaft. Iron head. A small golden sun stamped into the fletching.
Not an orc arrow. It never was.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: They hunted us like beasts.

lines.speaker: Grik
lines.text: Now I will hunt them.
End of the Prologue.
Chapter One: The Hunt.
